text:
zoe: hit a CI failure in sampleapp this morning after keys rotated for a customer. devs saw 401s on first run.

rahul: are they sourcing with env vars or using the CLI?

zoe: env vars. README shows REDWOOD_API_KEY but some of our old examples and docs still reference REDWOOD_KEY or REDWOOD_TOKEN. newcomers copied the old bits.

anya: we keep seeing subtle parity gaps across sdks 1. each SDK accepts a slightly different fallback list.

luke: small proposal: standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY + accept REDWOOD_KEY and REDWOOD_TOKEN as deprecated fallbacks (emit a one-line warning). update SDKs, sampleapps, and quickstarts.

zoe: good. also can we make the 401 surface actionable? "401 Unauthorized" isn't enough for support. at least hint at rotation/project-scope/env-var.

rahul: agree. map 401 from /v1/authorize to: "401 Unauthorized: possible causes include rotated key, project-scoped key, or wrong env var name. See devex onboarding checklist."

anya: i'll open a tiny PR for js + py sdks to normalize env resolution and the error message. luke, want sampleapp/docs?

luke: on it. i'll also add a CLI helper `rw auth export` that prints shell-friendly export lines to rehydrate env after rotation. low-risk UX.

cred-bot: rotation-evt: rotated by ops@newco at 2025-03-14T07:21:10Z; old_prefix=rw_old001; new_prefix=rw_new002; clients_impacted=2

zoe: nice. can we also add a support triage blurb: check env var name, check key scope (org vs project), and try `rw auth export` before reissuing keys. saves back-and-forth.

rahul: will add server-side metric tagging for rotation-suspected 401s when the key string matches legacy prefix patterns. helps find inbound affected clients.

anya: PRs incoming. linking them to the Acme ticket so support can notify customers once deployed.

luke: thanks all ":thumbsup:"
